transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I haven’t really been myself since my daughter left for basic training. I thought I’d handle it better, you know, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but the house just feels… dead when I come home.

I’ve been kind of falling apart more than I’d like to admit. Crying in my truck before shifts, messing up steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, snapping at the younger guys at work. And I don’t really go out on the water anymore or work on my sculpture. I used to love that stuff, but lately I just… don’t see the point. I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things that you used to find pleasurable, like working on your sculpture or going out on the water?

Yeah… I have. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but since my daughter left for basic training, it’s like I come home and the house just feels dead. I used to go out on the water to clear my head, or work on my sculpture, and now I just kind of look at it and think… what’s the point?

I know that probably sounds kind of pathetic. I just haven’t been able to keep myself together like I usually do.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day since your daughter left?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to say I’m depressed like… I don’t know, like I’m trying to make it sound bigger than it is. But since she left, most days I come home and it just hits me that the house feels dead.

I’ll think I’m holding it together, and then I’m crying in my truck before work, or I’m messing up basic steps on welding jobs I’ve done forever. I’ve been snapping at the younger guys too, which I’m not proud of. And I’m not going out on the water or working on my sculpture much at all anymore. I just kind of… don’t see the point lately. Is that what you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way most days — since your daughter left for basic training?

It’s been… about a month, I guess. Since she left for basic training. I kept thinking I’d settle down after a few days, but it’s been most days since then. I don’t know if that’s too short to be making a big deal out of it, but… yeah, about a month.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your daughter left for basic training?

Yeah… I guess I have. I don’t want to overstate it, but since my daughter left for basic training, it’s like I come home and the house just feels dead.

Most days I’m not really keeping it together like I should. I’ve cried in my truck before shifts, and I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. I’ve been snapping at the younger guys too, which I hate. And I’ve pretty much stopped going out on the water or working on my sculpture because I just… don’t see the point right now.

Is that what you mean by depressed most of the day?
Have you felt more fatigued or like you don’t have much energy lately, most days since your daughter left for basic training?

I’m not sure… I mean, I’m tired sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal, you know? My job can wear me out anyway.

I haven’t really been paying attention to it like that, most days. I can try to notice it more if that helps.
Have you found it harder to focus or think clearly lately, like when you're working on a welding job or making decisions at home?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do my job, because I usually can, but lately I’ve been missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. Stuff that should be automatic.

Since my daughter left, I come home and the house feels so empty, and I guess I’m not keeping myself together as well as I thought. I’ve cried in my truck before shifts, and then at work I’m not as sharp. I’ve snapped at the younger guys too, which I feel bad about.

So… yes, I guess focusing has been harder. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough, or blamed yourself for things more than usual lately?

I don’t know… maybe a little, but I don’t think I’d say I feel worthless or anything like that.

I do wonder if I should be handling all this better, like maybe I’m being too dramatic about my daughter leaving. But I haven’t really thought of it as blaming myself, exactly. I’m not sure if that answers what you’re asking.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

I… I don’t think so. Not like making a plan or wanting to hurt myself.

I’ve had moments where I’m just really overwhelmed and think, “I can’t keep feeling like this,” but I don’t think I mean I don’t want to be alive. I don’t want you to think I’m trying to be dramatic or anything. I’m just… having a hard time, I guess.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most or all of your usual activities, like work, hobbies, or spending time with people, most days since your daughter left for basic training?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in everything, exactly. I still go to work and do what I have to do.

But since my daughter left, when I come home it just feels like a dead house, and the stuff I used to do to unwind… I’m not really doing it. I haven’t been going out on the water, and I’ve barely touched my sculpture. I look at it and just kind of think, what’s the point?

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… most days, yeah, I guess I don’t get much pleasure out of things lately. Is that what you mean?
Have you found that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all of your usual activities, not just some, most days since your daughter left for basic training?

I guess… yes, more than I want to admit. I’m still showing up for work and doing the basic things, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely stopped functioning.

But when I get home, it feels like this dead house since my daughter left. I haven’t been going out on the water, and I’ve stopped working on my sculpture because I just kind of look at it and think, what’s the point? So… it’s not every single thing, maybe, but it feels like almost everything that used to help me doesn’t really do much for me now. Does that make sense?
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble functioning?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like this.

I mean, I’ve had bad weeks before, like anybody, and times where work was stressful or I was tired, but I don’t remember feeling this… stuck, I guess, or having it mess with me this much. At least not that I can think of.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you ever experienced a time in your life before this where you felt down most days, lost interest in things, or had real trouble functioning — not just normal stress or being tired, but something more serious like this?

No… I don’t think so. Not anything like this.

I mean, I’ve been sad before, and I’ve had rough stretches, sure. I don’t want to act like my life’s been perfect. But I can’t remember a time where it felt this heavy most days, or where I was having this much trouble getting myself to care about things.

At least… not that I’d call the same as this. Is that answering it right?
